Phuket Property Purchase Costs

Fees and taxes to budget for besides the price
HomeGuidesPhuket Property Purchase Costs

The price on a listing is not the only cost. This guide lists the usual cost items for buying a condo or villa in Phuket so you can ask the right questions. Rates below are the commonly applied ones; confirm the current rates and who pays what for your own deal.

Transfer fee

The Land Department charges a transfer fee, commonly 2% of the registered or appraised value of the property. In resale deals buyer and seller often split it, and new developments often have their own arrangement. It is negotiable, so make it explicit in the contract.

Stamp duty or specific business tax

Depending on how long the seller has held the property, either stamp duty (commonly 0.5%) or specific business tax (commonly 3.3%) applies, plus a withholding income tax for the seller. These taxes are usually the seller’s responsibility, but the contract decides.

Legal and agent costs

Budget for an independent lawyer to check the title, the contract and the developer. Fees vary; ask for a written quote. Our service for buyers is to answer questions and arrange viewings. Ask us about our terms directly.

Ongoing costs of a condo

Most condo projects charge a monthly or annual common-area maintenance fee and often a one-off sinking fund payment at transfer. Amounts differ by project and unit size, so ask the developer for the exact figures before you reserve. We list them on a project page only when the developer has published them.

Payment plan on new developments

A common off-plan structure is a reservation fee, a deposit when signing the contract and instalments linked to construction. Our standard reference structure is a THB 100,000 reservation, 20% on signing and the remaining 80% in construction-linked instalments. Each developer sets its own plan, so check the project page.

Checklist

  • Transfer fee: amount and who pays.
  • Taxes: stamp duty or specific business tax, and who pays.
  • Legal due diligence quote.
  • Common-area fee and sinking fund.
  • Furniture package and utility deposits, if not included.
  • Currency conversion and bank transfer charges.

General information only, not legal or tax advice, and rules can change. Confirm every point with a licensed Thai lawyer and the Land Department before you pay a deposit.

Sources: Thai Land Department, Thai Revenue Department
